examples.name: Wrapping a button
examples.description: The most common usage - wrap the one interactive child that needs a focus indicator.

examples.name: Suppressing the ring on a disabled control
Composing focusRingClassNames directly
examples.description: Used internally by components that need to add other classes to the same element - a raw input inside a custom control, for example.

antiExamples.name: Wrapping a non-focusable element
antiExamples.reason: FocusRing only styles :focus-visible - it does not make an element focusable. The child must already be a real native control or carry a tabIndex.

antiExamples.name: A local one-off focus rule
antiExamples.reason: Every interactive atom reuses this one primitive so the focus treatment is identical everywhere - a local rule fragments that consistency.
